unmapped_findings: Zener–Hollomon parameter at the sample condition (T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹) is lnZ = 58.69 (Table 1).

For the ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹ series the peak stress decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (a reduction of 82%); the value specific to 1000 °C is not tabulated (only the 900 and 1150 °C endpoints are given).

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T; peak stress can be lowered by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (applicable to this condition).
This sample's condition (1000 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹) falls within the regime (950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹) considered to yield a refined, uniform recrystallized grain structure.

The paper reports no sample-specific DRX average grain-size number for 1000 °C/0.01 s⁻¹; Fig. 10 only shows that the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve reaches just below 80 µm at 1150 °C and that at 900 °C all strain-rate curves lie between roughly 8 and 13 µm.
The same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch and composition were used to confirm reproducibility of the observed phenomena under identical experimental conditions.
